newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up on short covering.

text.p: Pakistani stocks surged past the 1,400-point barrier on Wednesday amid covering of short postions as talks between Pakistani officials and the International Monetary Fund began in Washington, dealers said.
They said the market was oversold and rumours that the talks may lead to a resumption of a stalled $600 million IMF standby loan facility prompted individuals to cover their positions.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 25.42 points, or 1.83 percent, to end at 1,410.85. Gainers led losers 174 to 73. Turnover rose to 16.85 million shares from 16.32 million on Tuesday.
Faysal Bank rose 0.40 to 21 rupees, Muslim Commercial Bank 1.10 to 35.85, Adamjee Insurance 2.0 to 87 and Cherat Cement 1.10 to 20.25.
Hub Power Co rose 1.10 to 31.50. PTCL rose 0.35 to 33.75. Fauji Fertilizer rose 1.75 to 70.50 and ICI Pakistan 0.50 to 18.
